descripcion: Brewery founded in 1691 north of the city of Nagano. Brews the Wakamidori label with prefecture rice and also sells alcohol-free amazake.
Sake brewery in the Shinonoi district of Nagano, label Motooinomatsu. Member of the prefecture's brewers' guild.
Brewery on the Kawanakajima plain in Nagano, label Katsuramasamune. Opens the kura to booked visits and has its own online shop.
Brewery founded in 1875 in Shinano-machi, at the foot of Mount Kurohime. Brews its whole range with Sankeinishiki rice grown under contract in the district, and also makes a yogurt liqueur.
Brewery founded in 1755 in central Obuse. Ferments in wooden vats and makes around 300 koku a year, among the smallest in the prefecture.
Suzaka brewery founded around 1873, label Keiryu. Makes the live nigori Domuroku and the Asashibori new-sake series.
Late-Edo brewery in central Komoro, five minutes from the station. Brews the Asamadake label.
Saku brewery with the Chikumanishiki, Yoshidaya Jisuke and Kiyama labels. Also makes shochu and rice liqueurs.
Brewery in the Iwamurata district of Saku, label Kanchiku. Member of the Nagano brewers' guild.
Saku brewery founded in 1891, label Miyamazakura. Beyond sake it makes shochu, wine, brandy, cider and liqueurs.
Brewery on the old Nakasendo road, in Motai. Thirty of its buildings are listed as national tangible cultural property, and it opens the kura to the public every March.
Brewery in Nakagome, Saku, label Kamenoumi. Works with pesticide-free rice grown in the district.
Brewery founded in 1901 in Nozawa, Saku. Brews Sawanohana with groundwater from the Yatsugatake system and prefecture rice.
Brewery in Usuda, Saku, brewing since the Genroku era. Has its own visitor room and offers guided kura tours by reservation.
Brewery in Shimogoe, southern Saku, label Sakunohana. Sells through appointed shops.
Brewery founded in 1858 in Yachiho, Sakuho, at 800 meters altitude on the upper Chikuma. Brews kimoto under the Izutsucho label.
Brewery founded in 1689 in Motai, Saku, wall to wall with Takeshige Honke. Its main label is Meikyoshisui.
Brewery on the Suwa kura walk, by the lake, label Reijin. Has its own online shop.
Brewery on the Suwa kura walk. Its flagship is the dry honjozo Taichi, alongside the junmai range of the Honkin label.
Brewery on the Suwa kura walk, label Yokobue. Releases limited seasonal editions and sells directly online.
Brewery founded in 1662 in Suwa, maker of Masumi. Beyond sake it makes alcohol-free koji amazake and runs tastings and seminars.
Brewery founded in 1871 in central Okaya by Kihinosuke Takahashi. Its range centers on dry, clean-drinking sake.
Shimosuwa brewery, label Mikotsuru. Its junmai daiginjo has taken gold medals at national and regional competitions through 2024.
Brewery founded in 1665 on Yanagimachi street, on the old Hokkoku road in Ueda. Brews the Shinshu Kirei label.
Brewery in Satoyamabe, east of Matsumoto, with some 150 years of history. Brews the Iwanami and Kyokasuigetsu labels and an amazake.
Brewery in central Matsumoto, label Fukashitsuru, named after the old Fukashi castle. Member of the Nagano brewers' guild.
Brewery in Toyoshina, Azumino, with some two hundred years of tradition. Its junmai daiginjo Donkura has taken eight consecutive Grand Gold awards at Monde Selection.
Brewery in Omachi, on the slopes of the Northern Alps, brewing with spring water from the range. Its current label is Ryusuisen, and it also makes lemon, plum and apple liqueurs.
Omachi brewery working local rice and Northern Alps water under the Hakubanishiki label. Sells directly from its own online shop.
Brewery in the city of Nakano with the Iwashimizu label, plus a modern range under its own names (Origine, Eclipse, Niwaringo). Takes orders from its own site.
Brewery in Nishiharuchika, Ina, founded in 1897. Draws Central Alps groundwater from 80 meters down and brews, among others, a 30-degree sake.
Brewery in Yawata, Chikuma, at the foot of Mount Obasute. Brews junmai only, under the Obasute Masamune label.
Brewery in Shinonoi, Nagano, label Shinanohikari. Shares a street with Higashiiida Shuzoten, at number 1724.
Brewery in the former village of Shinshushinmachi, west of Nagano. Its current label is Juku; it also retains the historic Misuzunishiki name.
Brewery in central Obuse, a few meters from Masuichi Ichimura. Brews the Hokushinryu label.
Brewery in the Iida district of Obuse, maker of Yonekawa and Hoga.
Brewery founded in 1637 beside Zenkoji temple. Since the 1990s it is the only maker of the collective label Unzan.
The Tokura house in Chikuma, member of the prefecture's brewers' guild. Its visible activity today is the soba restaurant Kaya and its shop.
Brewery in Senbonyanagi, Chikuma, label Tenpo. Member of the Nagano brewers' guild.
Brewery in central Nakano, maker of Ikioi Masamune.
The Yoshida house in Nakano, member of the prefecture's brewers' guild.
Brewery in Iiyama, in the snowy north of the prefecture, label Mizuo. Sells directly from its own online shop.
Brewery in Tokisato, Iiyama, label Hokko Masamune. Has its own online shop.
Brewery in Higashiyama, Nakano, at the mouth of the valley climbing to Shiga Kogen. Has its own online shop.
Ueda brewery with three hundred years of brewing, labels Fukumuryo and Go. Keeps its own shop, Sato no Kura, in a Taisho-era warehouse.
Brewery founded in 1896 on the Shioda plain, below the Bessho hot springs. Offers tastings at the brewery itself.
Brewery founded in 1887 on the old Hokkoku road where it crosses Ueda. Brews the Wadaryu label.
Brewery founded in 1867 in Mitakedo, Ueda. Its Sanada Rokumonsen label takes its name from the Sanada crest.
Brewery in Nagase, eastern Ueda, label Kikuzakari.
Brewery in Hiraga, Saku, maker of Kinpo Fuyo. Beyond sake it makes shochu.
Brewery in Osawa, Saku, with the sake label Hatsuuguisu and the shochu Tenyuki. Sells directly online.
Brewery in Honmachi, Okaya, label Miwatari, named after the ice phenomenon of Lake Suwa. Sells directly online.
Chino brewery, label Daiyagiku. Opened its own online shop in May 2026.
Brewery on the Suwa kura walk, fifth in the row, label Maihime. Has its own online shop.
Brewery in central Matsumoto, next to the castle. Brews with the Metoba no Izumi spring, which rises on its own plot.
Brewery in Shimauchi, Matsumoto, label Sasanohomare. Sells directly from its site.
Brewery in Shimadachi, Matsumoto, sole maker of the Daishinshu label, brewed with prefecture rice.
Brewery founded in 1869 in Shimadachi, Matsumoto, brewing with Northern Alps groundwater. Its labels are Alps Masamune and Kamenoyo.
Brewery founded in 1871 in Hirooka, Shiojiri, label Takanami. Sells directly online.
Brewery founded in 1883 in central Shiojiri. Works with rice grown under contract by local farmers and sells from its own shop.
Brewery in Seba, Shiojiri, beside the old Nakasendo road. Brews the Misuzu label.
The third brewery in the city of Omachi, brewing with Northern Alps water under the Hokuan Daikoku and Iizura labels.
Brewery in Aizome, Ikeda, named after the great snowfield of Mount Shirouma. Sells directly online.
Brewery founded in 1758 in central Ikeda, facing the Northern Alps, which give its label its name.
Brewery in the old post town of Ono, in Tatsuno. Its Yoakemae label takes the title of Toson Shimazaki's novel.
Brewery in Nakaminowa, Minowa, label Kishinomatsu.
Brewery founded in 1915 in central Ina, label Inokashira.
Brewery in Arai, Ina, label Shinano Nishiki.
Brewery in the old castle town of Takato, now part of Ina. Beyond sake it makes doburoku and amazake, and sells from its own shop.
Brewery in Komagane, at the foot of the Central Alps, label Shinanotsuru.
Brewery in Okusa, in the village of Nakagawa, in the Tenryu valley. Brews the Imanishiki label.
Brewery in Yabuhara, in the Kiso valley, by the Torii pass. Brews Kisoji and the Juroku-dai Kuroemon series.
Brewery in Kisofukushima, an old Nakasendo checkpoint, label Nanawarai.
Brewery in Kisofukushima, label Nakanorisan, a nod to the raftsmen who floated Kiso timber downriver.
Brewery in Suhara, in the village of Okuwa, on the lower Kiso. Its Kiso no Kakehashi label refers to the Nakasendo's hanging pass.
Brewery from the Iida area in the prefecture's guild, at the southern end of Nagano. Brews the Kikusui label.
